name: nnFoundation
plain: nnFoundation (DKFZ): self-supervised 3D encoders (a convolutional one and a vision transformer) pre-trained on 2.1 million CT, MRI and PET volumes; they turn a volume into feature maps for your own medical models. Share-alike weights (CC-BY-SA-4.0): fine-tuned models keep the licence.
summary: nnFoundation (Harsy et al. 2026): DKFZ's self-supervised 3D radiology foundation encoders, pre-trained with nnssl on 2.1 M CT, MRI and PET volumes. `nnfoundation-cnn` is the ResEnc-L U-Net encoder (6 stages, 32-320 channels, strides 1-32), `nnfoundation-vit` the Primus ViT (40 layers, width 1056, 8³ patch tokens, fixed 192³ input). Gives the encoder feature maps of a z-score normalised volume for fine-tuning or frozen-feature use; the MAE decoder is not included.

papers.title: Primus: Enforcing Attention Usage for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

limitations: CUDA portable and kernels accept stream=True to stage CNN levels or ViT blocks from pinned host memory. On the 192³ nnFoundation ViT reference, peak allocated memory during load and inference on an RTX 5060 Ti fell from 1,665 to 673 MiB in both modes.
Kernels peak allocated is equal to portable, but the cuDNN workspace next to the large conv maps (1.4 GiB and 0.3 GiB workspaces) fragments the allocator: peak reserved is ~580 MiB above portable.

A standalone fixed 192³ FP32 TensorRT ViT engine matched portable FP32 encoder features on eight CT crops. The standalone run took 7.02 s per crop with an estimated 8,452 MiB peak, versus 9.46 s and 2,864 MiB for portable FP32.
task_io: Input: a CT volume `[D, H, W]` in Hounsfield units and its voxel spacing in mm (`volume.read_nifti` reads both from a NIfTI file). Output: a class index per voxel `[D, H, W]` on the input grid (0 = background). Encoder models (nnFoundation) take a CT or MRI volume and give its encoder feature maps. For a trained nnU-Net v2 folder or checkpoint, see the [nnU-Net v2 loader](../api/volume.md#nnu-net-v2).

tensorrt.note: encoder only: excludes normalization, padding and output cropping; memory is an estimate combining non-PyTorch device usage and PyTorch peak; 192³ TensorRT checked against portable FP32 on eight real CT crops; 200³ ONNX was exported with an earlier same-shaped example before zero-padding was corrected and was subsequently checked on zero-padded input

quality.title: TotalSegmentator test subset (8 CT cases), encoder features vs the original fp32: cosine (worst case) / relative L2
quality.protocol: A small subset of real CT cases of the TotalSegmentator dataset (not the full test split), each run at its card's spacing (1.5 or 3 mm) in the same pipeline; mean over the cases of the Dice (0 to 1) averaged over the classes present, against the ground-truth segmentations (vertebrae_L6 of the subset has no counterpart and is skipped). Original = TotalSegmentator 2.18.0, default fp16 autocast. Encoder models have no task head, so they are judged by their output: the encoder feature maps against the original fp32 maps (cosine similarity, worst case over the cases and the mean over the maps; relative L2 error, mean). Original (fp32) is the reference; the original fp16 row shows the error the original itself has in half precision.

original16.note: encoder features vs the original fp32 (original fp32 (GPU)), 6 feature maps, cosine (min over cases) and relative L2 (mean)

portable.note: encoder features vs the original fp32 (original fp32 (GPU)), 6 feature maps, cosine (min over cases) and relative L2 (mean)

kernels.note: encoder features vs the original fp32 (original fp32 (GPU)), 6 feature maps, cosine (min over cases) and relative L2 (mean)

portable32.note: Compared 6 feature maps per CT case against the pinned upstream FP32 encoder.

tensorrt.note: Fixed 192-cubed FP16 engine with eager z-scoring and padding. Six feature maps per CT compared against the pinned upstream FP32 encoder.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.8e-06 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.15 % and p99 <= 1.1 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `features`).
